## Research question

A clinical database interface must distinguish unsupported questions from answerable requests and SQL-generation errors without rejecting valid answers merely because they are zero or empty.

## Method

A logistic-regression classifier uses schema/content overlap, initial-word patterns and question length. Accepted questions pass to fine-tuned T5-3B, then an execution-result inspector can replace the SQL with a refusal token.

## Evaluation

The EHRSQL 2024 shared-task study reports separate local validation protocols and four leaderboard submissions with different mistake penalties. The released README targets MIMIC-IV demo data. Question-classifier validation approximates the inferred test refusal prevalence; the generator uses an i.i.d. SQL-pair split.

## What the results support

The final system reports 68.9 Accuracy0, 56.5 Accuracy5 and 44 Accuracy10, but a strongly negative AccuracyN. The tested GPT-4 debugging variant worsens results, with removed conditions noted in error analysis. The authors explicitly acknowledge false refusals of otherwise correct results and weak distribution-shift robustness.

## Limits and qualifications

Local component scores and penalty-free leaderboard scores are not safety guarantees. Feature and prevalence choices use leaderboard information. The result filter rejects valid zero/None outputs, and the released runner makes a batch-level fixed-quota decision. The paper’s multiplication of component probabilities assumes error independence without demonstrating it. No interactive clarification or clinical deployment evaluation is reported.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

An inspectable answerability baseline illustrating the difference between conservative filtering, correctly detecting unsupported requests and preserving legitimate empty or zero answers.
